summary: A dense, tightly-optimized worker-placement game where your workers must first study disciplines before they can perform stronger actions, layering a skill-development puzzle on top of pick-up-and-deliver ship movement around the Galápagos. Turns feel purposeful and interlocking, but the sheer number of subsystems (contracts, species collection, exploration cards, boat routes, worker training) makes early plays heavy and slow.
praised: Innovative worker-progression/skill-training system layered onto worker placement
Gorgeous, thematic production (islands, ship miniature, wooden bits)
Deep, satisfying engine-building and route optimization
Meaningful long-term planning across contracts and exploration
criticised: High rules overhead and iconography, steep learning curve
Long playtime, especially first few games
Can feel dry/cerebral with limited table talk
Similar 'multiplayer solitaire' feel to Luciani's other worker-placement designs (Barrage, On Mars)
Analysis paralysis due to many simultaneous optimization paths

interaction.kind: worker-placement space-blocking (claim action), otherwise mostly parallel play

scoring.why: Points accumulate from fulfilled contracts, species/set collection, exploration progress, and endgame bonuses, so the winner is usually whoever balanced several scoring engines rather than maxing one.
